title: CT deep-learning radiomics model classifies osteoporotic vertebral fracture types
summary: A ResNet-50 deep transfer-learning model (RadImageNet versus ImageNet pretraining) fused with radiomics features classified osteoporotic vertebral fractures into three ASTLOF classes in 981 patients (1,098 vertebrae) from three centres. Macro-AUC for the RadImageNet fused model was 0.837 versus 0.648 internally, 0.773 versus 0.633 externally and 0.852 versus 0.648 in the prospective cohort (n = 51). External and prospective cohorts are small and training macro-AUCs of 0.934 versus 0.996 suggest overfitting.
ai_technology: ResNet-50 deep transfer learning (RadImageNet versus ImageNet) fused with radiomics, LASSO and eight machine-learning classifiers
organization: Sir Run Run Hospital, Nanjing Medical University

evidence.tested: Internal (n = 187), external (n = 110) and prospective (n = 51) validation cohorts from three centres against an MRI-based ASTLOF reference.
evidence.unknown: Frozen-model status of the prospective cohort and clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep transfer learning and radiomics features classified fracture types on CT.
